title: Westville and Lincoln's Funeral Train, May 1, 1865

sources.what: 'On Monday May 1, 1865, shortly before 8:00 a.m., the train bearing the body of President Lincoln stopped briefly at this site'; erected 1965 by the Westville Women's Club; W. Main St. and Monon St.
sources.who: Westville Women's Club marker (1965), via the Historical Marker Database

sources.who: Flickr (speedyjr), Indiana Historical Marker - Lincoln's Funeral Train, Westville

sources.what: 'The train passed through Westville at about 20 minutes to 8 a.m.'; Willie Lincoln's casket on the train; Michigan City: 'a magnificent arch of roses and evergreen'; the train waited an hour or so there for the Chicago committee
sources.who: Fern Eddy Schultz, LaPorte County Historian, What's New LaPorte (2009)

beats.text: A murdered president's funeral train came through Westville.
beats.label: WESTVILLE, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: Westville Women's Club marker (1965); Indiana Historical Bureau

beats.text: On May 1, 1865, it rolled north from Indianapolis through the night, past mourners lit by bonfires and torches.
beats.label: MAY 1, 1865

beats.text: Shortly before 8 in the morning, it reached Westville.
beats.label: SHORTLY BEFORE 8 A.M.
beats.credit: Westville Women's Club marker (1965); county historian Fern Eddy Schultz

beats.text: Westville's 1965 marker says the train stopped briefly here.
beats.label: WESTVILLE

beats.text: His son Willie, who died in 1862, made the trip with him.
beats.label: THE FUNERAL CAR
beats.credit: TIME; American Battlefield Trust; Illinois History and Lincoln Collections

beats.text: Up the line, in Michigan City, the train stopped beneath an arch of roses and evergreens.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY
beats.credit: Indiana Historical Bureau; county historian Fern Eddy Schultz

beats.text: Later that morning, Lincoln left Indiana, where he grew up, for the last time.
beats.label: MAY 1, 1865
beats.credit: Indiana Historical Bureau; National Park Service

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: First script pulled: the 2,000 people, bareheaded men and silent women, white flags, arch of evergreens and roses and the choir singing 'The Departed' come from a Chicago Tribune passage that the Monon Society places at Michigan City (the county historian's 2009 article places it after Westville). Sources disagree, so the Westville short now keeps only what is solid for Westville (the marker's 'shortly before 8 a.m.', the LaPorte Herald's 'tremendous crowd at the depot'), puts the arch in Michigan City, adds Willie Lincoln on the train, makes the last line 'Later that morning', drops the dawn sky (8 a.m. was full daylight) and draws nine cars at night. Second check: the LaPorte Herald 'tremendous crowd' line rests on one 2009 article, so line 4 now cites the 1965 marker ('stopped briefly'); 1865 reports call the Michigan City morning clear, so the grey sky became a clear morning.
